card.name: Semicolons in old narrative prose
card.fires_on: The semicolon (or closing parenthesis plus semicolon) ending a full clause in old-style historical or scientific prose. The next clause usually begins with "and", "but" or a new subject.

modes.label: Semicolon before and/but
modes.description: A semicolon ends a clause about events or battles, and a contrasting or continuing clause follows.
modes.example: Memnon, thinking their forces insufficient to oppose Alexander, recommended that they should retire and lay waste the country behind them<< ;>> but his advice was overruled.

modes.label: Semicolon after citation
modes.description: A closing parenthesis with a semicolon follows a bracketed reference in a historical account.
modes.example: Achilles came up, and killed Memnon (Diet. Cret. iv. 6<<);>> the same accounts represent Antilochus

card.plain: It marks a semicolon that joins two long clauses in old history or science writing.
